notes:
CRM notes:
- Account: Stonebridge ReserveWorks (payments & fraud analytics for B2B SMBs).
- Focus: move chat + doc search workloads off shared hosted to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost.
- Primary ask: dedicated capacity sizing workshop to validate baseline QPS and token/sec requirements, agree latency SLOs and throughput guarantees for an enterprise contract.
- From AE call 2026-02-20 (Samira): 'we need a predictable tail latency and clear burst model — spikes around month-end crush us today'.
- Security: strict data residency for EU clients (must have audit logs, KMS integration). Infosec wants SAML SSO + SOC2 evidence before pilot.
- Workshop objectives: measure baseline QPS (steady-state), characterize peak vs steady-state, map average tokens per response, recommend reserved GPU count and instance types, define autoscale/burst rules, draft SLA language (p95/p99 latency, throughput guarantees, credits).
- Preliminary metrics provided by customer: typical daytime steady-state 45 req/s; average response payload ~180 tokens; expected peak events ~200-250 req/s lasting 10-30 minutes during settlement windows.
- Calculated tokens/sec (workshop input): steady ~8.1k t/s (45 * 180), peak ~45k t/s (250 * 180). Customer skeptical of numbers; wants Redwood to validate with load test.
- Redwood workshop recommendation (draft): target p95 latency < 200ms for chat (conservative), p50 < 50ms; throughput guarantee: baseline 50 req/s guaranteed, burst pool for up to 300 req/s with pre-warm and fallback to smaller model variants.
- HW guidance: 6 x H100-80GB for headroom w/ int8 quantized LLM variant OR 10 x A100-40GB if customer requires NVidia A100 fleet. Recommend split pool: steady reserved + burst on demand.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — wants unit economics analysis (tokens/second cost + model mix recommendations). Ask from CFO: target < $0.0008 per generated token across traffic mix.
- Pilot proposal: 6-week dedicated pilot, limited to EU and NA regions, instrumented with Redwood Console dashboards and evals. Deliverables: latency & cost baseline, recommended reserved sizing, SLA draft.
- Legal/procurement notes: procurement prefers a 12-month commitment with quarterly SLO reviews. Infosec asked for sample SOC2 report and encryption at rest proof (KMS).
- Quote/links: workshop deck in Drive (linked). Open Jira for initial infra questions: INF-4820 (VPC peering), INF-4951 (quantization profile testing).
- Sales choreography: AE -> finalize scope -> SE runs sizing workshop -> engineer load tests -> present sizing & SOW -> procurement negotiation.
- Quote: 'We really need no surprises on latency during peak settlement — that's our top risk' (VP Eng, 2026-03-04).
